note: input.ops is a script run in a fresh directory; expected is {files, results}; a case that must fail adds error_op_index and still records files and results, because for a refusal the directory is the assertion. results lists only the queries that SUCCEEDED, and is [] rather than null when there are none, so the port never has to tell an empty list from an absent one. A query value is the loaded *Config re-marshaled by encoding/json, so it is the loader's whole decision, not a projection. write_file puts a literal file in the directory with no code involved; load reads the named file through LoadConfig; defaults calls DefaultConfig without touching the disk; save writes the config from the last load or defaults call back out through SaveConfig, and save refuses to run without one rather than inventing a config to write. files maps every file left in the directory to its exact bytes, with the eight date digits of a MakeBackup suffix replaced by <date> because they are wall-clock. No error text is recorded anywhere: the Go message quotes the absolute path of the file it failed on. A case that saves the same file twice adds save_stable, whether the second save produced the identical document, because a config that drifts on every start is a property of the code and not of the machine. Every case runs with HOME fixed at /home/oracle and PICOCLAW_* cleared, so a workspace path in the expectation is the loader's expansion and not the generator's environment.
